$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-SEV-004 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §9.5 and the RF-SEV-004 inventory entry. Mixed-source rule. Expresses proximal/full-thickness injury benchmark and PROHIBITION structure only: pooled operative and nonoperative timelines are broad research benchmarks only (evidence_record_only); treatment selection, individual timing, surgery, and autonomous management choice are prohibited. When management restrictions are unresolved, it DEFERS to RF-SAF-006 and blocks generic rehabilitation; it never overrides RF-SAF-006. No diagnosis, surgical advice, treatment/timing logic, raw-media interpretation, autonomous prognosis engine, deterministic formula/score, confidence, phase, rehab, plan, or return-to-sport logic; safety precedence preserved. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.

input_contract.$comment: Structural benchmark inputs taken verbatim-in-meaning from v1.2 §9.5. Pooled operative/nonoperative timelines are broad research benchmarks only; proximal/full-thickness status is used only when documented, never inferred; raw media is never interpreted here.

decision_contract.$comment: Benchmark + prohibition structure only. Benchmarks are guarded research context (evidence_record_only); treatment selection, individual timing, surgery, and autonomous management are prohibited. When management restrictions are unresolved, defer to RF-SAF-006 and block generic rehabilitation; never override RF-SAF-006. No diagnosis, raw-media interpretation, deterministic formula/score, numeric values, phase/rehab/plan/RTS. Safety precedence preserved.

notes: Mixed normative source; MUST. Dual/contextual permitted_use in the body: evidence_record_only for benchmarks; prohibited_autonomous_rule for treatment selection or individual timing — the inventory/object record the primary permitted_use (prohibited_autonomous_rule) and the dual role is captured structurally in decision_contract (benchmark_role / autonomous_use_status). Architecture refs and evidence claims preserved per source: architecture V3.1-6 (anchor quality), V3.1-13.1 and V3.1-13.2 (prescription gate / missing-input behaviour), V3.1-20 (referral-resolution lifecycle); QRF-012 (C1), QRF-032 (C1), QRF-036 (I1), each bounded to its exact source-supported benchmark/context role and not generalized into autonomous treatment or prognosis authority. Per §9.5 logic: pooled operative and nonoperative timelines are broad research benchmarks only. Per §9.5 decision: when management restrictions are unresolved, apply RF-SAF-006 and block generic rehabilitation (this rule defers to RF-SAF-006 and never overrides it). Per §9.5 prohibited use preserved exactly: no treatment-superiority inference, no individual return prediction, no autonomous management choice. Proximal/full-thickness status is used only when documented by an acceptable external report or verified assessment, never inferred from mechanism, pain location, symptoms, self-tests, or raw imaging; raw media is not interpreted here and requires a separately validated imaging subsystem (V3.1 §25). Cohort benchmarks remain group context only, never individual prediction; the rule creates no deterministic prognosis/severity/recurrence/treatment-decision score, assigns no confidence/probability, determines no rehab phase, authorizes no rehab, produces no complete plan or return-to-sport decision, and does not override safety, current capacity, external restrictions, stage, readiness, or concurrent-injury constraints. Uncertainty is preserved when the source is weak, absent, user-entered without source, unclear, non-specific, not externally reported, or not documented as required. Prognosis rule that defers to the safety block, so safety_state_output is null and blocked_targets is empty; the actual rehabilitation block is owned by RF-SAF-006. No severity/prognosis model is authored here (deferred to the later severity and readiness objects). Draft — approval_status remains pending.
